# Unit specs that stub document and window at module level lose them to a neighbour's teardown

## Context

Promotes @neo-opus-grace's defect-note of 2026-09-25 10:51Z (fingerprint on the A2A bus): `DomEvents.spec.mjs:149` threw `document` undefined at `DomEvents.mjs:829` and `Touch.spec.mjs:126` threw `window is not defined` at `Touch.mjs:122`, both on attempt 1 of run 36054057269, both green on retry. Second occurrence today on PR #19214 (`eacf70ada0`, a Workstation-only diff): run 36135015416 was red on attempt 1 at `grid/StoreInteractions.spec.mjs:270` (a count assertion, a different class) and on its rerun at the same DomEvents/Touch pair — through all of CI's retries, because a retry runs in the same worker with the same clobbered globals. The whole suite is green locally at that head (4,589, no failure), where the worker count and the interleaving differ.

## The Problem

The unit suite runs `fullyParallel` on four CI workers, and a worker imports many spec files into one process. Eight specs write `globalThis.document` (and some `globalThis.window`) as a stand-in for the main thread. Two of them install the stub at **module level** and rely on it for the whole file — `test/playwright/unit/main/DomEvents.spec.mjs` (document and window) and `test/playwright/unit/main/draggable/sensor/Touch.spec.mjs` (window; its document is per test). Their neighbours capture `originalDocument = globalThis.document` at **their** import time and restore it in `afterAll` or `afterEach`, deleting the global when the original was undefined. When such a neighbour imported before the victim and its teardown runs while the victim's tests are still pending in the same worker, the victim's stub is gone: `document.body` throws in `getLocalWheelTarget`, `window.scrollX` throws in the touch sensor's release path. Order-dependent by construction, which is why reruns flip.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs`: `fullyParallel: true`, `workers: 4` on CI, `retries: 2`.
- Module-level installers: `DomEvents.spec.mjs` lines 23–24, `Touch.spec.mjs` lines 47–48 (document per test through `installDocument()`, window once), also `main/DomAccessAlign.spec.mjs` (document only) and `main/addon/ResizeObserver.spec.mjs` (re-installs in a hook).
- Import-time-original restorers: `dashboard/DockFlip.spec.mjs`, `main/addon/InputModality.spec.mjs`, `main/addon/GoogleMapsReadiness.spec.mjs`, `worker/ManagerReplySettlement.spec.mjs`, and `Touch.spec.mjs` itself.

## The Fix

The victims own their stubs per test: `DomEvents.spec.mjs` and `Touch.spec.mjs` re-install their own `document` and `window` references in `test.beforeEach` (idempotent, the same objects the module-level code created, so the sensor's import-time listener registration stays valid). The teardowns keep restoring. No production code changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 Both specs re-install their document and window stubs in `beforeEach`; deleting the globals between two of their tests no longer fails the next test (a red-first arm in each spec deletes both globals in a preceding test).
- [ ] AC-2 The unit suite is green on CI at the PR head, and PR #19214's rerun on a `dev` that carries this fix is green.

## Out of Scope

The `grid/StoreInteractions.spec.mjs:270` count assertion (a separate timing class, defect-note `e01b99180c6d70fe`); `DomAccessAlign.spec.mjs`, which installs at module level but has not been observed failing — the same hook is a one-line follow-up if it does.
